title: GMAT Focus Quant Practice Test 2
instructions: GMAT Focus Edition Quantitative Reasoning: 21 Problem Solving questions, 45 minutes. An on-screen calculator is permitted.

questions.prompt: £4,620.00 is divided between three people in the ratio 4 : 5 : 5. How much does each of the two larger shares receive?
questions.explanation: The ratio has 14 parts, so one part is £4,620.00 / 14 = £330.00. Each larger share is 5 parts, £1,650.00; the smaller share is £1,320.00.

questions.prompt: Two trains start 468 km apart and travel toward each other at 96 km/h and 84 km/h. After how long do they meet?
questions.explanation: Closing speed is 96 + 84 = 180 km/h, so the gap of 468 km closes in 468 / 180 = 2.6 hours. Using either speed alone gives the wrong answer.

questions.prompt: A machine costing £24,000.00 loses 18% of its value each year, calculated on its value at the start of that year. What is it worth after 3 years?
questions.explanation: Each year multiplies the value by 0.82: £24,000.00 × 0.82³ = £13,232.83. Subtracting 18% of the original three times would give £11,040.00, which is too low because later years apply the percentage to a smaller base.

questions.prompt: Four of five test scores are 62, 71, 55, 80. The mean of all five is 68. What is the fifth score?
questions.explanation: The five scores must total 68 × 5 = 340. The four known scores total 268, so the fifth is 72.

questions.prompt: A circular table has a radius of 7 metres. What is its area, to the nearest square metre?
questions.explanation: Area is πr² = π × 7² = 153.9, which rounds to 154 square metres. The circumference, 2πr, is 44 metres and is the usual confusion.

questions.prompt: A rectangular gate measures 9 m by 12 m. How long is a diagonal brace across it?
questions.explanation: The diagonal is √(9² + 12²) = √(81 + 144) = √225 = 15 m. Adding the sides gives 21 m, which is longer than any straight line across the rectangle.

questions.prompt: Two machines are serviced every 12 days and every 18 days respectively, and were both serviced today. In how many days will they next be serviced on the same day?
questions.explanation: The next common day is the lowest common multiple of 12 and 18. Their highest common factor is 6, so the LCM is (12 × 18) / 6 = 36 days. Multiplying the two intervals gives 216, a common day but not the first.

questions.prompt: A component fails on any given day with probability 0.15, independently of other days. What is the probability that it fails at least once in three days?
questions.explanation: Work with the complement: it survives all three days with probability 0.85³ = 61.4%, so it fails at least once with probability 38.6%. Adding 15% three times gives 45%, which double counts the days it fails more than once.

questions.prompt: A bill of £570.00 includes VAT at 20%. What is the amount before VAT?
questions.explanation: The bill is 120% of the net amount, so the net is £570.00 / 1.2 = £475.00. Taking 20% off the total gives £456.00, which is wrong because the 20% was added to the smaller figure.

questions.prompt: Two painters can finish a job alone in 9 hours and 12 hours respectively. They work together for 3 hours, then the faster one leaves. How much longer does the second take to finish?
questions.explanation: Together they complete 1/9 + 1/12 = 7/36 of the job an hour, so in 3 hours they finish 58.3%. The remaining 41.7% at 1/12 an hour takes 5.0 hours.

questions.prompt: A culture of 250 cells doubles every hour. How many cells are there after 6 hours?
questions.explanation: Doubling 6 times multiplies by 2⁶ = 64: 250 × 64 = 16,000. Multiplying by 2 and then by 6 gives 3,000, which treats the growth as linear.

questions.prompt: A car uses 6.4 litres per 100 km. Fuel costs £1.48 a litre. What does a 275 km journey cost, to the nearest penny?
A driver travels for 2 hours at 45 km/h and then 3 hours at 70 km/h. What is the average speed for the whole journey?
questions.explanation: Total distance is 90 + 210 = 300 km over 5 hours, giving 60 km/h. The unweighted average of the two speeds is 57.5, which ignores the longer time at the higher speed.

questions.prompt: How many integers between 17 and 96 inclusive are divisible by 7?
questions.explanation: The multiples of 7 in range run from 21 to 91: 21, 28, … 91. That is (91 − 21)/7 + 1 = 11 values. Forgetting to add one is the usual slip.

questions.prompt: Eight readings have a mean of 62. A ninth reading of 89 is added. What is the new mean, to one decimal place?
questions.explanation: The eight readings total 496. Adding 89 gives 585 over 9 readings: 65.0. Averaging the old mean with the new value gives 75.5, which weights one reading as heavily as eight.

questions.prompt: A committee of 3 is to be chosen from 9 candidates. In how many ways can it be formed?
questions.explanation: Order does not matter, so the count is 9 × 8 × 7 / (3 × 2 × 1) = 84. The figure 504 is 9 × 8 × 7, which counts each committee six times, once for each order.

questions.prompt: A rectangle's length is increased by 20% and its width is reduced by 10%. By what percentage does its area change?
questions.explanation: Area scales by 1.20 × 0.90 = 1.08, an increase of 8%. Adding the percentages to get 10% ignores that the two changes multiply.

questions.prompt: Units cost £3.20 each, or 15% less per unit on orders of 500 or more. What is the smallest order for which buying exactly 500 units costs less than buying 480 units at full price?
options: The larger order always costs more
questions.explanation: 480 units at full price cost £1,536.00. 500 units with the discount cost 500 × £3.20 × 0.85 = £1,360.00, which is less despite being more units.

questions.prompt: Town A spends £128,000.00 on libraries for 46,000 residents; Town B spends £96,000.00 for 30,000 residents. Which spends more per resident, and how much more?
options: They spend the same per resident
questions.explanation: Per resident: Town A £2.78, Town B £3.20. Town B spends £0.42 more per head, even though Town A spends £32,000.00 more in total.

questions.prompt: A business reports revenue of £84,000.00 and a profit margin of 22.5% of revenue. What is its profit?
questions.explanation: Profit is 22.5% of £84,000.00 = £18,900.00. The figure £65,100.00 is the cost, not the profit.

questions.prompt: £6,500.00 earns simple interest at 4.2% a year. After how many whole years does the balance first exceed £8,000.00?
questions.explanation: Interest is £273.00 a year, so reaching £1,500.00 of interest takes 5.49 years. The balance first exceeds the target after 6 whole years.
